assign.request: Critic B, the systems designer, second visit. Read the REBUILT paging code and docs (public/imagine/paging/: paging.js, words.js, the rail, the library, the toolbar, the drawer, doc/*) and answer: are the six blocks now one name, one control and one page each (list the remaining synonyms with file:line); does a reader cross blocks (layouts x navigation x appearance x hierarchy) anywhere - say exactly where and what is missing; is 'the realm is one configurable page' true in the code (how many code paths draw a stage; how many places define the surface words; how many times navigation is defined); what 'infinite potential' would mean here concretely and the one seam that would unlock it. End with a ranked one-line FIX LIST. Fix nothing.

log.msg: SCOPE READ (rebuilt realm): paging.js 224, blocks.js 172, stage.js 343, toolbar.js 138, config.js 160, presets.js 107, rail.js 85, block.js 90, content.js, page.js 134, library/page.js 84, the six block pages, toolbars/page.js, plus the survivors build/ make/ mechanisms/ navigation/ templates/ critique/ inventory/, readme.md and doc/*.md (1736 lines). paging.css is 1009 lines, 175 distinct classes.

Q1 NAMES - NAVIGATION is still defined FIVE times, and three of them are live writers. blocks.js:32 NAVIGATION (6 values, the intended one) - build/words.js:44 NAVS (6, imported by build/page.js:7) - words.js:11 MECHANISMS (4, re-exported at paging.js:10 and WRITTEN to page.json by make/page.js:320) - make/tabs.js:28 KIDS (2, written by make/page.js:321) - stage.js:64 a hardcoded literal of the six ids. Sibling realm layouts/system.js:71 is a sixth list of different words. doc/decisions.md:84 claims all three were merged; they were not.

Q1 NAMES cont - SURFACES defined five times: blocks.js:102 - build/words.js:89 (its own comment admits the copy) - layouts/system.js:38 - templates/families.js:55 TONE (a translation) - stage.js:60 a literal. ARRANGEMENT three times: blocks.js:79 (7 values) - build/words.js:101 ARRANGES (4) - stage.js:63 literal. CONTENT three times: blocks.js:54 (8) - build/words.js:113 BLOCKS (3) - make/made.js:52-60, which still carries the DELETED xs-xl rungs.

Q1 CONTROLS - two control surfaces, not one. The hover toolbar (toolbar.js:42-59: five dropdowns + two colour rows) is the one for the demo half. The editor half has its own: build/page.js's seven picture-choosers over build/words.js, and make/page.js:318-321's four word chips. They edit different key names for the same ideas.

Q1 PAGES - five of the seven config keys have a page. blocks.js:143 DEFAULT has seven keys; BLOCKS (:124) declares six blocks, five with an axis. `background` and `type` have toolbar controls and NO page and NO url: block.js:70 routes only `this.axis`, and skin/page.js:19 sets axis 'surface', so /imagine/paging/skin/display/ and /skin/ for the page colour do not exist. Also two pages named Stage: /paging/stage/ (the block) and /paging/navigation/stage/ ('Reserved stage').

Q2 CROSSING - the crossing DOES exist and it is the hover toolbar itself: seven controls over one live stage, on every page that calls this.stage(). What is missing is HIERARCHY, the owner's fourth axis. The word 'hierarchy' appears exactly ONCE in the whole realm, at templates/theming/page.js:96. That page - 5 surfaces x 3 type scales, fifteen cells at once - is the only side-by-side comparison in the realm besides navigation/lab.js, and it is NOT in the rail (rail.js:48-53 lists four Templates tiles, not theming). Every other page shows one stage, so comparing two arrangements is an act of memory.

Q3 ONE CONFIGURABLE PAGE - readme.md and doc/decisions.md:76 say 'there is no second renderer'. There are SEVEN code paths that draw a stage: stage.js:26 PagingStage - build/stage.js:26 BuildStage (208 lines, its own tabs/rail/crumbs/blocks) - mechanisms/swap/swap.js:56 PagingSwapper - navigation/lab.js:30 PagingNavLab and :182 PagingNavStack - navigation/screen.js:27 PagingNavScreen (a SECOND app shell beside paging.js:138 Realm) - demos.js:36/63/105/124 (four miniatures) - make/tabs.js:41 tabs_items. Only templates/templates.js goes through the real seam (stage's `draw`).

Q3 THE REAL BREAK - TWO SCHEMAS INTO ONE STORE. config.js:130 writes mode:{navigation,content,room,arrangement,surface,background,type}; make/page.js:318-321 writes mode:{style,content,mech,kids}. make/page.js:91 `if (mode.navigation) return {...DEFAULT,...mode}` means a page made by the drawer IGNORES every chip Make shows on its row - click one and it writes `style` and nothing on screen changes. And made.js:52-60 seeds content 'xs|s|m|l', none of which are in CONTENT, so make/page.js:102 falls all four seeded pages back to 'article' and the first chip click jumps to the head of a different list.

Q3 DEAD WORDS - `axes:` survives on 15 pages (navigation/page.js:35, navigation/stage:18, navigation/tabs:23, navigation/columns:60, ten templates/*/page.js, theming:60) with ZERO consumers anywhere in the repo. `width:` survives on five (build/page.js:56 'full', make/page.js:113 'large', critique:146, inventory:19, theming:59) and is meaningless in the app's middle - their layout headers still describe 'a column in /imagine/'s row', a container they no longer have. paging.css carries ~30 class names no js references (paging-teach*, example*, place-*, swapped*, still, steps, brick*, sample, shown, word, cell, calls, reset, change, note, line, group, center, postwall, side-*).

Q4 INFINITE POTENTIAL, CONCRETELY - the vocabulary already spans 6 nav x 8 content x 4 room x 7 arrangement x 5 surface x 5 background x 3 type = 100,800 pages. The realm exposes about 43 of them: 12 presets (presets.js), 27 single-value urls (block.js:70), 4 toolbar edges. The other 100,757 are reachable by clicking but UNSENDABLE: grep for location/searchParams/hash across the realm returns nothing but two location.reload() calls in baseline.js. So a reader who finds a shape nobody anticipated cannot link it, bookmark it, or show it to anyone, and decision 4 (correctly) throws it away on refresh.

Q4 THE ONE SEAM - PUT THE CONFIGURATION IN THE URL. Paging.stage() (paging.js:121) reads the seven words off the query string on mount; PagingStage.set() (stage.js:282) writes them back with one history.replaceState. That single seam makes all 100,800 addressable, turns a preset from a module entry into a bookmark, makes `nest` a word in the url instead of drawer-only state, gives the hub's route() one branch that can answer ANY configuration, and turns 'make this a page' from a dev-socket file write into 'copy this link'. It is the only change that lets a reader PRODUCE something the authors did not anticipate and keep it.

FIX 8 - BuildStage renders a PagingStage - build/stage.js:26 - hand it a config instead of re-implementing tabs, rail, crumbs and blocks; this is what makes 'one renderer' true rather than stated - L

assign.outcome:
**The rebuild is real, and the realm is one configurable page for the half a reader sees. The other half never moved.** Read-only audit of the rebuilt `public/imagine/paging/`. Nothing was changed.

**What is genuinely true now.** One vocabulary file, `blocks.js`, imports nothing and feeds the rail, the toolbar, the drawer, the urls and the docs. One hover toolbar with seven controls over one live stage IS the crossing the owner asked for (layouts × navigation × appearance), and it is on every page that calls `stage()`. Twelve presets with real urls and no directories. Two independent colour controls. The drawer's nest and "make this a page".

**What the docs claim and the code does not.** `readme.md` and `doc/decisions.md` both say "there is no second renderer". There are **seven** code paths that draw a stage — `stage.js:26` · `build/stage.js:26` · `mechanisms/swap/swap.js:56` · `navigation/lab.js:30` and `:182` · `navigation/screen.js:27` (a second app shell) · `demos.js` (four miniatures) · `make/tabs.js:41`. Navigation is defined **five** times and three are live writers (`blocks.js:32`, `build/words.js:44`, `words.js:11`, `make/tabs.js:28`, plus a literal at `stage.js:64`). Surfaces **five** times, arrangement **three**.

**The one real break.** Two schemas write one store: the drawer writes `{navigation, room, arrangement, surface, background, type}` (`config.js:130`), Make writes `{style, content, mech, kids}` (`make/page.js:318-321`). `make/page.js:91` short-circuits on `mode.navigation`, so **clicking a chip on a drawer-made page changes nothing** — silently. The seed pages still carry the deleted `xs`–`xl` rungs and all four render `article`.

**Missing.** `background` and `type` have controls but no page and no url. "Hierarchy" — the owner's fourth axis — appears once in the whole realm, at `templates/theming/page.js:96`, on the only side-by-side wall there is, which the rail does not link.

**Infinite potential, concretely.** The vocabulary already spans **100,800** pages. About **43** have urls. The rest are reachable by clicking and impossible to send — there is no `location`, `searchParams` or `hash` anywhere in the realm.

**The one seam: put the configuration in the url.** `stage()` reads the seven words off the query on mount, `set()` writes them back with one `replaceState`. That makes all 100,800 addressable, turns a preset into a bookmark, makes `nest` linkable, and turns "make this a page" from a dev-socket write into "copy this link". It is the only change that lets a reader keep a page nobody anticipated.
